problem: Producing films needed large funding and Marvel had limited resources.
title: Marvel borrows $525 million against its characters to make its own films
context: Marvel had licensed its characters to studios and decided to produce films itself.
decision_made: Take a $525 million non-recourse credit facility from Merrill Lynch secured by film rights to ten characters.
action_taken: Later amended the facility to cover Iron Man and The Incredible Hulk; accounts differ on whether Iron Man was funded by the facility or by Marvel's own money.
observed_outcome: Iron Man reportedly earned over $500 million, and Marvel's later film business grew. Kevin Feige said Merrill Lynch likely could not have provided the financing from 2008 onward.
lessons: Using intellectual property as collateral can fund a studio strategy, but it ties the company's future to the films' success.
limitations: Accounts disagree on the facility term (seven or eight years) and on Iron Man funding. Several sources are commentary, and the box office figure is from a secondary article.

claims.claim_text: Marvel obtained a $525 million non-recourse credit facility from Merrill Lynch secured by film rights to ten characters.
ScreenCrush reported that Iron Man made over $500 million and the strategy paid off.
